## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
**Stable to rising.** Q1-2026 was cautious on .web ("nothing substantive that's new"); Q2-2026 shifted to clear confidence after delegation; Q3-2026 opened with "strong results ... both operationally and financially" and was specific on .web dates. 2026 revenue guidance: $1.730-1.745B (2026-02-05) -> $1.745-1.755B (mid-year) -> $1.755-1.760B (2026-10-22). Domain-base guidance raised at every 2026 call. Management guides conservatively and raises; the 43% EPS beat rate in our metrics reflects tight consensus around a very predictable business, not missed promises. **Reliability: High.**

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
- Retail registrar pricing has moved only about 1% since the April notice; analysts asked whether a step-up near the effective date will hurt renewals. Management: no meaningful early renewals seen ahead of 2026-11-01.
- Q4 component trends (gross adds, deletes): management declined to guide components, citing holiday seasonality.
- VeriSign Informed unit economics: no answer beyond "follow the microsite."
- Not asked on this call but material: the Cooperative Agreement with the US Commerce Department that caps .com pricing, and the renewal of the .com registry agreement (2030). These are the long-dated risks.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
- Red: free cash flow down 14% y/y in Q3-2026 and lower over the trailing year than FY-2025, despite revenue growth.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
- The phrase "high assurance" is new framing that ties DNS reliability to a broader trust-services pitch (VeriSign Informed). It suggests management is looking for a second growth leg as .com volume growth eventually normalizes.

# VeriSign (VRSN) - a deep dive on management and the setup

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

VeriSign runs the registries (the master databases) for .com and .net under contracts with ICANN (the body that coordinates internet names) and the US Commerce Department. It cannot sell to the public; it sells each name wholesale to registrars such as GoDaddy, at a price the contract caps.

Across these five calls the story moved from "the domain base has stopped shrinking" to "the domain base is growing at the fastest rate in a decade."

- **Q3 2025 (2025-10-23):** the tone was relief. The improved trends "that emerged at the end of 2024 continued through the first 3 quarters of 2025." Management first credited AI tools with "increases in registration and resolution activity." Much of the call was spent defending against worries (parked-domain advertising, the long legal fight over .web).
- **Q4 2025 (2026-02-05):** 2025 closed with the base up about 4.5 million names to 173.5 million. The 2026 guide for base growth was a cautious 1.5% to 3.5%, with revenue guided to $1.715B-$1.735B.
- **Q1 2026 (2026-04-23):** management gave notice of a $0.71 rise in the annual .com wholesale price, from $10.26 to $10.97, effective 2026-11-01. Revenue guidance went up to $1.730B-$1.745B.
- **Q2 2026 (2026-07-23):** "the largest [new registrations] we have seen for any quarter in our history," and .web was delegated into the root zone with VeriSign as registry operator, ending a dispute that ran for years. Management said new products had not been "put on hold."
- **Q3 2026 (2026-10-22):** base at 183 million names, up 6.1% from a year earlier; a record 13.1 million new registrations in the quarter; base-growth guidance raised again, to 6.5%-7%. Two new growth lines now have dates: .web (a 30-day sunrise period, the window when trademark holders register first, from mid-December 2026; general availability around April 2027) and VeriSign Informed, a certificate-revocation checking service announced 2026-10-05, with pricing promised by year-end and availability in the first half of 2027.

The arc is expansion. A one-product toll-road story has picked up two optional new products, but the economics are still almost entirely .com.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Demand for domain names is accelerating | Base +6.1% year on year to 183M (2026-10-22); new registrations 13.1M against 10.6M a year earlier | Corroborated |
| Revenue grows with base and price | FY revenue $1.33B (2021) to $1.66B (2025), about 5.2% a year over three years; Q3 2026 +5.7% | Corroborated, but growth stays mid-single-digit |
| Guidance is reliable and rising | Revenue guide raised from $1.715B-$1.735B (Feb) to $1.730B-$1.745B (Apr) to $1.755B-$1.760B (Oct) | Corroborated |
| Strong cash generation funds returns | FCF (free cash flow, cash from operations minus capital spending) was $1.07B in FY2025; trailing twelve months (TTM) to 2026-09-30 is $1.02B. Q3 2026 FCF was $261M against $303M a year earlier, which the CFO put down to "higher cash taxes and payments to employees and vendors" | Partly corroborated: FCF is falling while revenue rises |
| Shareholder returns | $1.14B returned in the last twelve months, more than the $1.02B of TTM FCF; cash fell from $618M (Q3 2025) to $476M (Q3 2026); net debt about $1.31B ($1.79B borrowings less $476M cash) | Returns now run ahead of cash generation |
| Earnings growth | Q3 2026 diluted EPS $2.35 ($2.41 before a $0.06 write-down on assets held for sale) against $2.27; TTM EPS $9.30; latest-quarter EPS up about 4% year on year | Slower than the full-year +10% |

The core claims hold up. The one softer number is cash: FCF is lower than a year ago while revenue is higher. Higher cash taxes explain it, not weaker demand. Even so, cash per share is not compounding as fast as the domain base right now, and buybacks are partly funded from the balance sheet.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY - Rising

- Q3 2025: careful and defensive ("the traditional use of domain names isn't going away").
- Q4 2025: measured; a wide, conservative base-growth guide.
- Q1 2026: confident enough to take a price rise.
- Q2 2026: "record metrics," .web resolved, products back on the agenda.
- Q3 2026: "the factors driving the solid domain name base trends ... further accelerated." The CEO also answered the renewal-rate question directly: first-time renewals run "in the forties," later renewals "in the mid eighties," and the new cohort falls into "the best renewing ... cohort, the online presence cohort."

Guidance has become narrower and more specific over the year, which is a sign of confidence.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY - High

Base-growth guidance went from 1.5%-3.5% (Feb 2026) to 6.5%-7% (Oct 2026), and revenue and operating-income guidance were raised at every call. Management under-promises at the start of each year. The screener's EPS "beat 3 of 7 quarters" is not a credibility problem: the misses are by a cent or so against consensus (Q3 2026 was $2.41 ex-charge against a $2.42 estimate), while VeriSign's own guidance has been beaten repeatedly. Reliability: High.
